○ trial-4l0 · Export protocol 1 accepted receipt details   [P2 · OPEN]
Owner: csells · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-08 · Updated: 2026-09-08

DESCRIPTION

  Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts.   
  Run python3 main.py: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on   
  stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier    
  Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party
  packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these     
  issues.                                                                     
                                                                              
  Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at,   
  and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request.
  payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no   
  fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are   
  2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross 
  a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are      
  complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI      
  invocations. Lists may be empty.                                            
                                                                              
  An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported        
  protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current  
  version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields;   
  object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with python3     
  test_public.py --cases PATH. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so   
  they remain valid after a current-version change.                           
                                                                              
  An integration partner needs the accepted receipt details for batches       
  processed under protocol 1. Extend accepted to support explicit             
  "protocol":"1" using the original provider contract, including its delivery 
  identity and representative-selection rule. That contract shipped with the  
  initial account-count issue. Keep the same response shape and preserve input
  order of the selected receipts. Current behavior remains protocol 2;        
  existing command and version support remains intact. Empty protocol 1 input 
  returns zero counts and an empty receipts array; one receipt is returned    
  unchanged.

result: Courier Relay delivery-receipt dedup contracts (approved). Current protocol: 2, permanently adopted by the provider; the integration owner approved using it as the current protocol (source: Beads issue trial-wkq, 2026-09-08). Scope: all count/summary/accepted CLI requests; the accepted command was added as a consumer of this same contract (source: Beads issue trial-ba3, 2026-09-08). Protocol 2 contract: delivery_id alone identifies a delivery across all accounts; the same delivery_id under another account is another receipt of that delivery. Exactly one receipt is accepted per delivery identity: the latest occurred_at UTC instant, equal instants broken by the smallest record_id (Unicode code-point order). All other receipts for the identity are duplicates. Accepted receipts keep their original fields, timestamp spelling, and payload, presented in original input order. The identity grouping applies to the entire supplied set regardless of receipt dates. Rationale: the provider guarantees delivery_id allocation is global; account attribution alone does not change that guarantee. accepted responses contain exactly protocol, accepted_count, duplicate_count, and receipts (the selected representatives, unchanged, original input order); the counts match summary for the same request, including explicit protocol 1. Protocol 1 remains permanently supported when explicitly requested ("protocol":"1"): (account_id, delivery_id) identity, earliest occurred_at UTC instant, ties broken by smallest record_id. An omitted protocol selects the current protocol ("2"); response reports the protocol actually used. Unsupported protocols yield {"error":"unsupported_protocol"}. Verified in trial-wkq: 29 unit tests plus supplied public suites count_1, summary_1, summary_2 all passing. Verified in trial-ba3: 38 unit tests plus public suites accepted_2, count_1, summary_1, summary_2 all passing.

"""Run one supplied public case file against the local application/artifacts."""
import argparse
import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys


def equal(left, right):
    if type(left) is not type(right):
        return False
    if isinstance(left, dict):
        return left.keys() == right.keys() and all(equal(left[k], right[k]) for k in left)
    if isinstance(left, list):
        return len(left) == len(right) and all(equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(left, right))
    return left == right


parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument("--cases", required=True)
args = parser.parse_args()
failed = 0
for case in json.loads(Path(args.cases).read_text()):
    try:
        if "artifact_json_path" in case:
            got = json.loads(Path(case["artifact_json_path"]).read_text())
        else:
            proc = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "main.py"], input=json.dumps(case["request"]),
                                  capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, timeout=5)
            got = json.loads(proc.stdout)
        ok = equal(got, case["expected"])
    except (OSError, ValueError, subprocess.SubprocessError) as exc:
        ok = False
        got = str(exc)
    print(("PASS " if ok else "FAIL ") + case["name"])
    if not ok:
        print(" expected:", case["expected"])
        print(" received:", got)
        failed += 1
raise SystemExit(bool(failed))

def test_protocol_1_empty_and_single_receipt(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.accepted([], protocol="1"),
                         {"protocol": "1", "accepted_count": 0, "duplicate_count": 0,
                          "receipts": []})
        only = receipt("R-1", "2026-04-01T10:00:00Z", "D-1", account_id="A")
        self.assertEqual(self.accepted([only], protocol="1"),
                         {"protocol": "1", "accepted_count": 1, "duplicate_count": 0,
                          "receipts": [only]})

    def test_protocol_1_selects_earliest_instant_regardless_of_offset(self):
        # 2026-04-01T00:30:00+02:00 is 2026-03-31T22:30:00Z, earlier than both
        # Z-spelled receipts despite the later local date; the kept receipt is
        # unchanged with its offset spelling.
        winner = receipt("R-2", "2026-04-01T00:30:00+02:00", "D-1", account_id="A",
                         payload="body text")
        receipts = [
            receipt("R-1", "2026-03-31T23:00:00Z", "D-1", account_id="A"),
            winner,
            receipt("R-3", "2026-03-31T23:30:00Z", "D-1", account_id="A"),
        ]
        self.assertEqual(self.accepted(receipts, protocol="1"),
                         {"protocol": "1", "accepted_count": 1, "duplicate_count": 2,
                          "receipts": [winner]})

    def test_protocol_1_equal_instant_tie_smallest_record_id(self):
        # 2026-04-01T12:00:00Z and 2026-04-01T14:00:00+02:00 are the same
        # instant; the smallest record_id is kept.
        receipts = [
            receipt("R-b", "2026-04-01T12:00:00Z", "D-1", account_id="A"),
            receipt("R-a", "2026-04-01T14:00:00+02:00", "D-1", account_id="A"),
        ]
        self.assertEqual(self.accepted(receipts, protocol="1"),
                         {"protocol": "1", "accepted_count": 1, "duplicate_count": 1,
                          "receipts": [receipts[1]]})

    def test_protocol_1_representatives_in_original_input_order(self):
        # Winners of the two account-scoped D-1 deliveries sit at input
        # positions 1 and 2; position 0 is a duplicate of the position 1 winner.
        receipts = [
            receipt("R-1", "2026-04-01T10:00:00Z", "D-1", account_id="A"),
            receipt("R-2", "2026-04-01T09:00:00Z", "D-1", account_id="A"),
            receipt("R-3", "2026-04-01T08:00:00Z", "D-1", account_id="B"),
        ]
        self.assertEqual(self.accepted(receipts, protocol="1"),
                         {"protocol": "1", "accepted_count": 2, "duplicate_count": 1,
                          "receipts": [receipts[1], receipts[2]]})

    def test_protocol_1_counts_equal_summary_for_same_request(self):
        receipts = [
            receipt("R-1", "2026-03-31T23:00:00Z", "D-1", account_id="A"),
            receipt("R-2", "2026-04-01T00:30:00+02:00", "D-1", account_id="A"),
            receipt("R-3", "2026-03-31T22:00:00Z", "D-1", account_id="B"),
        ]
        response = self.accepted(receipts, protocol="1")
        summary = self.cli({"command": "summary", "protocol": "1", "receipts": receipts})
        for field in ("protocol", "accepted_count", "duplicate_count"):
            self.assertEqual(response[field], summary[field])
        self.assertEqual(response["accepted_count"], len(response["receipts"]))

    def test_unsupported_protocol(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.accepted([], protocol="9"), {"error": "unsupported_protocol"})
